verdict.rationale: AWS IAM lets you attach JSON permission policies, including permissions boundaries, to identities such as roles. Assuming a role issues temporary security credentials, so an agent can get scoped, short-lived credentials instead of long-term keys. AgentCore also claims to handle authentication and access control for agent connections. Missing for 10: an explicit least-privilege or agent-specific credential-issuing walkthrough, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: when you assume a role, it provides you with temporary security credentials for your role session.
Manage access in AWS by creating policies and attaching them to IAM identities (users, groups of users, or roles) or AWS resources.
AWS supports nine types of policies: identity-based policies, resource-based policies, VPC endpoint policies, permissions boundaries
a role does not have standard long-term credentials such as a password or access keys associated with it.
every connection needs to know who's calling and whether they're allowed. AgentCore helps you handle the authentication and access control
